hints: Focus on what is happening to bonds in each step, are you breaking a strong bond or just joining two very reactive species?
Label each equation first as initiation, propagation or termination, remembering that initiation breaks $Cl-Cl$ and propagation breaks $C-H$ or $Cl-Cl$.
Think about why joining two radicals together to make a new bond releases energy straight away and needs almost no push to get started.
walkthrough:
**Recall the three stages**

Think of the mechanism like starting, keeping going, and stopping. Initiation makes radicals, propagation keeps radicals going, termination removes radicals.

$$\text{Initiation: } Cl_2 \rightarrow 2Cl\bullet$$
$$\text{Propagation: radical + molecule } \rightarrow \text{ new radical + molecule}$$
$$\text{Termination: radical + radical } \rightarrow \text{ molecule}$$

**Compare bond breaking and bond making**

Breaking bonds always needs energy input, so it has a real activation energy. Making a bond releases energy, so it is much easier to start.

Initiation A breaks the $Cl-Cl$ bond with UV light. Propagation B breaks a $C-H$ bond in $C_2H_6$. Propagation C breaks a $Cl-Cl$ bond in $Cl_2$.

**Spot the radical combination**

Option D is $Cl\bullet + C_2H_5\bullet \rightarrow C_2H_5Cl$. No bonds are broken here, only a new $C-Cl$ bond is formed.

$$Cl\bullet + C_2H_5\bullet \rightarrow C_2H_5Cl$$
Two highly reactive radicals combining has almost zero activation energy, so this termination step is the fastest and lowest energy barrier.

options.A: This is initiation by homolytic fission of $Cl_2$. Breaking the $Cl-Cl$ bond needs a large input of UV energy, so it has a high activation energy, not the lowest.
options.B: This is the first propagation step. A $C-H$ bond in ethane must be broken to form $HCl$, which is relatively strong and needs significant activation energy.
options.C: This is the second propagation step. A $Cl-Cl$ bond must be broken to form $C_2H_5Cl$. Although easier than breaking $C-H$, it still needs activation energy to break a bond.
options.D: This is a termination step by radical combination. Two radicals join to form a $C-Cl$ bond with no bonds broken, so bond formation releases energy and the activation energy is essentially zero, the lowest of all.
